comparisons.peer_topic: Intellectual Property Enforcement and Protection Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel cannot always protect or enforce its IP rights due to litigation uncertainties, geopolitical factors, and compulsory licensing regulations, which may harm its competitive position. The theft of trade secrets and inadequate IP protection for innovations also pose risks to the value of R&D investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Intel disclose risks related to their ability to protect and enforce intellectual property rights, but they differ in operational focus. Qualcomm reports active enforcement actions, having initiated litigation against Transsion in multiple jurisdictions to enforce IP rights against unlicensed products. In contrast, Intel discusses general enforcement risks and limitations, noting it 'cannot always protect or enforce' its IP due to litigation uncertainties and geopolitical factors, without citing specific active lawsuits in this context.

sentences.text: While we continue to engage in negotiations toward a comprehensive resolution, we have initiated litigation against Transsion in multiple jurisdictions to enforce our intellectual property rights against certain of its unlicensed products.
We cannot always protect our IP or enforce our IP rights.
Our ability to enforce these rights is subject to general litigation risks, as well as uncertainty as to the enforceability of our IP rights in various countries and other geopolitical factors.
